title: Patch
description: An installable patch/update from a content source (Phase 5) — the thing a deployment actually installs, as distinct from an advisory (why it matters). Global content, NOT tenant-scoped (docs/adr/0010-global-content-catalogue.md). Known fields are closed; per-source extras go in the open 'sourceMetadata'.

source.description: The source that PUBLISHES the installable update. Excludes 'nvd' (describes vulnerabilities, not fixes) and 'kev'/'epss' (scoring overlays) — none of them ship a patch. All three remain valid inside 'provenance'.

vendorId.description: The vendor's patch identifier, e.g. KB5034441, USN-6789-1, RHSA-2025:0001. Unique per (source, vendorId).

reversible.description: Whether the patch can be uninstalled/rolled back. GATES ROLLBACK (Phases 8/9) — an irreversible patch may reach deploy-failed but never rollback-in-progress. Set at ingestion where known and finalised at assessment; DEFAULT false when unknown, because false is the safe answer (phase-1.md 'Reversible/irreversible flag', DIFFERENTIATORS #1).

requiresReboot.description: Whether applying this patch requires a reboot. Feeds the blast-radius dry run's reboot count and maintenance-window estimate (DIFFERENTIATORS #3). Default false when unknown.

classification.description: Vendor's own category, raw as sourced (e.g. 'Security Updates', 'Critical Updates', 'Driver'). Not normalized — sources disagree on taxonomy.

withdrawnAt.description: Set when the vendor pulls the patch (it happens). Content retires; it is never deleted.

supersedes.description: Vendor ids of patches this one supersedes. Persisted as edges in patch_supersedence; at assessment each missing patch resolves to its effective head (HARD-PROBLEMS #4). Cycles are detected and broken defensively by Phase 6 — the DB only rejects self-loops.

provenance.description: REQUIRED. One entry per contributing source — same shape as advisory.schema.json, so 'which source told us this patch is reversible?' is always answerable.

feed.description: Any feed we ingest — broader than the patch 'source' enum, because a source can contribute provenance without publishing the update itself.

sourceMetadata.description: Open extension point — per-source fields that do not belong in the normalized contract (e.g. wsusscn2 applicability rules, MSRC product ids), carried without a frozen-contract change.
